slides.title: The prompt
slides.text: The prompt Look at this paper: “Impacting spheres: from liquid drops to elastic beads” (Soft Matter 2026), PDF attached. The source code is github.com/comphy-lab/Soft-Sphere-Impacts. Clone it and follow its AGENTS.md. Clock: record date -u now and at each milestone; report the total at the end. 1. Reproduce Figure 5(a). Use $basilisk-master and $basilisk-runs. Simulate the infinite-Weissenberg (Kelvin–Voigt) case, bounce-kv.c, at We = 100 and El = 40 (Ec = 4000), at grid level 9: coarse, but enough for a first comparison. Digitise F (t) from Figure 5(a) and compare the two with $publication-plots, stating the relative error in Fmax and in its time. Add a drop-impact video coloured by velocity. 2. In parallel, find the Bingham (viscoplastic) model in github.com/comphy-lab/MultiRheoFlow and implement it here: twoPhase-VP.h with the plumbing it needs, and bounce-bingham.c, following the existing drivers. Run one Bingham case at We = 100 with yield stress J = τy /(ρV 2) = 0.001 and add its F (t) to the plot. 3. Fully document bounce-kv.c, the driver behind the soft-matter paper. Be concise and to the point. 4. Combine everything on one branch. Get $council-of-sages approval (seats gpt-6.2-astra at medium effort and claude-fable-5-2 at high; two rounds are enough if both seats score above 7), then $gh-pr-create a normal PR. $full-stop: never merge. Rules: simulations through $research-compute-dispatch on my lab workstation, inside my published reservation (8 cores, 32 GiB). I authorise running while it stays held: give each run half its cores, 4 threads each; skip activation, tracker updates and release, and book nothing else. If it is unavailable, you may stop one of my lower-priority simulations, never a registered or production run, and record exactly what you stopped. The PR carries code and documentation only (it is public). Report the plot, the video, the PR link and the timings.

slides.title: How to access HPC and shared resources securely?
slides.text: How to access HPC and shared resources securely? 1 Prepare the job package locally 2 Read and approve the scripts 3 Let the agent run only these scripts 4 The agent submits and polls while you sleep

slides.title: A script you can read in a minute
slides.text: A script you can read in a minute # submit Full scripts id=$(ssh "$host" "cd '$dir' && sbatch --parsable '$script'") [[ $id =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 1 # a job ID, nothing else # poll until it leaves the queue for _ in $(seq 288); do [ -n "$(ssh "$host" "squeue -h -j $id")" ] || break sleep 300 done # how did it end? ssh "$host" "sacct -n -X -j $id -o JobID,State,Elapsed" Teaching excerpt. The full scripts also validate inputs, handle lost replies and failed queries, and bound resubmission.
